entries.title: Normalized common-vertex overlap of layered paths
entries.statement: For two paths P and Q each visiting n vertices with one vertex in each of the same n time layers, their normalized common-vertex overlap is |P intersect Q|/n. A probability of changing the path measures whether this overlap is below one at all; it does not by itself measure how far below one it is.
assumptions: Paths use one vertex in each of the same n layers

entries.title: Draft counterexample to a change-based power-variance bridge
entries.statement: DRAFT AUTHOR RESULT; INDEPENDENT REFEREE AND MODEL-PROVENANCE GATES PENDING. For each N>=3 take a fixed iid N(0,1) origin and N layers of N iid N(0,1) sites, all weights independent, with all edges between consecutive layers. Every path has n=N+1 vertices and a free endpoint. The maximum has variance Theta(N/log N), failing every fixed n^(1-epsilon) upper bound. Under independent Gaussian OU perturbation at time N^(-1/2), the maximizing path changes with probability tending to one while common-vertex overlap divided by n tends to one in expectation and probability. This is a triangular sequence of growing-degree complete layered graphs. It refutes only a general auxiliary implication using path replacement alone, even with an O(n/log n) variance premise; it does not refute the unrestricted planar lattice problem or a bridge assuming actual quantitative overlap decay. The proof is in the linked campaign artifact; current novelty and parent openness are UNKNOWN.
assumptions: Graph width and degree grow with N
Independent standard Gaussian weights and OU copies at every site
Author proof awaits w500 independent check

relations.rationale: The counterexample contrasts the probability of any path replacement with the stated normalized common-vertex overlap; both ends specify equal layer counts.
